Laws of Set Algebra: Idempotent, Associative, Commutative, Distributive, Identity, De Morgan's Laws
Principle of Duality in Set Theory and Boolean Structures
Partially Ordered Sets (Posets): Partial Order Relation (Reflexive, Anti-Symmetric, Transitive)
Hasse Diagrams: Visualizing Posets, Construction Rules, Covering Relations
Extremal Elements in Posets: Maximal, Minimal, Greatest (Maximum), and Least (Minimum) Elements
Bounds in Posets: Upper Bounds, Lower Bounds, Least Upper Bound (LUB / Supremum / Join), Greatest Lower Bound (GLB / Infimum / Meet)
Lattices as Algebraic Systems: Definition as Poset where every Pair has LUB and GLB (a v b, a ^ b)
Properties of Lattices: Idempotency, Commutativity, Associativity, Absorption Laws
Special Lattices: Distributive Lattices, Complemented Lattices, Bounded Lattices
Boolean Algebra Foundations: Definition as a Complemented Distributive Lattice (B, +, *, ', 0, 1)
Uniqueness of Finite Boolean Algebras: Isomorphism to Power Set Boolean Algebra (Cardinality 2^n)
Boolean Functions & Boolean Expressions: Truth Values, Sum-of-Products (SOP), Product-of-Sums (POS) Normal Forms

units.title: Propositional Logic, Predicate Calculus & Mathematical Proofs
topics: Propositions: Declarative Statements, Truth Values (True/False), Atomic vs Compound Propositions
Basic Logical Connectives: Negation (NOT ~), Conjunction (AND ^), Disjunction (OR v)
Conditional (Implication ->) and Biconditional (<->) Statements: Truth Tables, Antecedents and Consequents
Converse, Inverse, and Contrapositive of Conditional Statements: Logical Equivalence Proof of Implication and Contrapositive
Truth Tables for Complex Logical Formulas: Construction and Step-by-Step Evaluation
Tautologies, Contradictions, and Contingencies: Definitions, Truth Table Identification
Logical Equivalence: Equivalence Laws (Identity, Domination, Double Negation, De Morgan's Laws for Logic)
Algebra of Propositions: Simplifying Boolean Propositional Expressions using Logical Equivalences
Rules of Inference: Modus Ponens, Modus Tollens, Hypothetical Syllogism, Disjunctive Syllogism, Resolution
Valid and Invalid Arguments: Fallacies, Testing Argument Validity via Truth Tables and Derivation Rules
Predicate Logic & Propositional Functions: Variables, Predicates P(x), Domain of Discourse
Quantifiers: Universal Quantifier (For All), Existential Quantifier (There Exists)
Negation of Quantified Statements: De Morgan's Laws for Quantifiers (~(For All x P(x)) <=> There Exists x ~P(x))
Normal Forms in Propositional Logic: Disjunctive Normal Form (DNF) and Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF)

units.title: Combinatorics, Recurrence Relations & Binomial Theorem
topics: Fundamental Principles of Counting: Addition Principle (Rule of Sum) and Multiplication Principle (Rule of Product)
Factorial Notation: n!, Properties, Recursive Definition 0! = 1
Permutations: Linear Permutations of n Distinct Objects, Formulas P(n, r) = n! / (n - r)!
Permutations with Repetition: Objects Not All Distinct (n! / (n1! * n2! * ... * nk!))
Circular Permutations: Arrangements in a Circle ((n - 1)! for Distinct Sense, (n - 1)! / 2 for Reversible)
Combinations: Selection without Regard to Order, Formula C(n, r) = n! / (r! * (n - r)!)
Combinatorial Identities: Symmetry Identity C(n, r) = C(n, n-r), Pascal's Identity C(n, r) + C(n, r-1) = C(n+1, r)
Binomial Theorem for Positive Integral Index: Statement, Expansion Formula, Pascal's Triangle Geometry
Key Terms in Binomial Expansions: General (r+1)th Term Formula T_{r+1} = nCr * a^(n-r) * b^r
Determination of Middle Term(s) in Binomial Expansion (n is Even vs n is Odd)
Term Independent of Variable (Constant Term) and Finding Specific Coefficients in Expansions
Pigeonhole Principle: Basic Statement, Generalized Pigeonhole Principle, Applications to Discrete Sets
Recurrence Relations: First-Order and Second-Order Linear Homogeneous Recurrence Relations with Constant Coefficients
Solving Recurrence Relations: Characteristic Equation Method, Fibonacci Sequence Closed-Form Derivation

units.title: Algebraic Structures & Group Theory
topics: Binary Operations: Definition on a Set, Closure Property, Commutativity, Associativity, Distributivity
Identity and Invertible Elements: Existence of Unique Identity Element, Inverse of an Element
Algebraic Structures Hierarchy: Groupoids (Closure), Semigroups (Closure + Associativity)
Monoids: Semigroups with Identity Element, Matrix and String Monoids
Groups: Definition, Four Group Axioms (Closure, Associativity, Identity, Inverses)
Abelian (Commutative) Groups: Definition, Examples (Integer Addition (Z, +), Real Multiplication (R*, *))
Finite Groups and Group Order: Order of a Group |G|, Order of an Element o(a), Group Multiplication Tables (Cayley Tables)
Subgroups: Definition, Necessary and Sufficient Conditions for a Subset to be a Subgroup (Two-Step and One-Step Subgroup Tests)
Cyclic Groups: Generator Elements, Properties of Cyclic Groups, Subgroups of Cyclic Groups
Cosets: Left Cosets (aH) and Right Cosets (Ha), Properties of Cosets, Partitioning of Group into Disjoint Cosets
Lagrange's Theorem: Statement (Order of Subgroup Divides Order of Finite Group), Proof and Corollaries
Normal Subgroups: Definition (gH = Hg for all g in G), Criterion for Normal Subgroups, Quotient (Factor) Groups
Group Homomorphisms: Definition (f(ab) = f(a)f(b)), Kernel of Homomorphism, Group Isomorphisms (Fundamental Theorem)
Burnside's Lemma / Theorem: Orbits, Stabilizers, Orbit-Counting Theorem for Combinatorial Symmetries
Applications of Group Theory to Coding: Binary Symmetric Channels, Group Codes, Generator and Parity-Check Matrices

units.title: Graph Theory, Trees & Network Algorithms
topics: Graph Fundamentals: Definition G = (V, E), Vertices, Edges, Directed Graphs (Digraphs) vs Undirected Graphs
Graph Terminology: Adjacent Vertices, Incident Edges, Degree of a Vertex (deg(v)), In-degree and Out-degree
Handshaking Theorem (Euler): Sum of Degrees of all Vertices = 2 * |E|, Proof and Corollaries (Number of Odd Vertices is Even)
Types of Graphs: Simple Graphs, Multigraphs, Pseudographs (Self-Loops and Parallel Edges)
Special Families of Simple Graphs: Complete Graphs (K_n), Cycle Graphs (C_n), Wheel Graphs (W_n), Regular Graphs (k-regular)
Bipartite Graphs: Definition, Characterization (Graph is Bipartite iff it has No Odd Cycles), Complete Bipartite Graphs (K_{m,n})
Subgraphs, Isomorphic Graphs, and Homeomorphic Graphs: Invariants of Graph Isomorphism
Walks, Trails, Paths, and Cycles: Connected Graphs, Connected Components, Cut-Points (Articulation Points) and Bridges
Eulerian Graphs: Eulerian Trail, Eulerian Circuit, Euler's Theorem (Connected Graph is Eulerian iff Every Vertex has Even Degree)
Hamiltonian Graphs: Hamiltonian Path, Hamiltonian Cycle, Dirac's Theorem and Ore's Theorem Criteria
Planar Graphs: Euler's Planar Formula V - E + F = 2, Non-Planar Graphs, Kuratowski's Theorem (K_5 and K_{3,3})
Graph Coloring: Vertex Coloring, Chromatic Number chi(G), The Famous Four Color Theorem
Tree Fundamentals: Definition as Connected Acyclic Graph, Equivalent Characterizations of Trees (n vertices, n-1 edges)
Spanning Trees: Definition, Existence in Connected Graphs, Fundamental Cycles and Fundamental Cutsets
Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) Algorithms: Kruskal's Greedy Algorithm (Disjoint Set Union) and Prim's Algorithm
Matrix Representations of Graphs: Adjacency Matrix (A), Properties of Adjacency Matrix Powers, Incidence Matrix (M)
